prompt.context: Our client, American Bank, is a national retail bank operating in the US. ATMs have traditionally been a profitable channel, but the bank has started seeing declining operating profits from its ATMs. The CEO has hired your firm to help her analyze the reasons for this decline and solutions to improve usage.
prompt.question: How would you approach this problem?

clarifying_info.q: How long have profits been declining?
clarifying_info.a: Profits have been declining over the last 5 years (2013–2018).

clarifying_info.q: How significant is the ATM channel to the bank?
clarifying_info.a: ATMs contribute to 12% of the bank's revenues.

clarifying_info.q: Which geographies do the ATMs operate in?
clarifying_info.a: ATMs are operated in the US only.

clarifying_info.q: Has the number of ATMs changed?
clarifying_info.a: There are 12,000 ATMs; no change in number or operating structure over the last 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: How does the bank operate its ATMs?
clarifying_info.a: Three operating structures: Bank Owned & Bank Operated (BO-BO), Bank Owned & Vendor Operated (BO-VO), and Vendor Owned & Vendor Operated (VO-VO). For VO-VO, the bank earns a commission on transactions.

clarifying_info.q: Who can use American Bank ATMs?
clarifying_info.a: Any person — own bank customers and other bank customers — can use any American Bank ATM.
Up to 5 competitors observed in the vicinity of any ATM.

exhibits.title: American Bank ATM Usage, Profits and Revenues in Last 5 Years
exhibits.shows: Two charts. Left chart shows total average daily hits per ATM across the US from 2013 to 2018, broken down by Own Customer hits and Other Customer hits. Right chart shows total profits and total revenues from ATMs (in millions of dollars) from 2013 to 2018.
exhibits.data: Daily hits per ATM: 96 (2013), 94 (2014), 92 (2015), 89 (2016), 87 (2017), 85 (2018). Revenue ($M): $1.88 (2013) declining to $1.62 (2018). Profit ($M): $1.15 (2013) declining to $0.89 (2018). Own customers make up a larger share of hits than Other customers. Note: 'hits' = number of unique times an ATM was used.

exhibits.title: American Bank ATM Fall in Hits Across US (2018)
exhibits.shows: A US map shading each state by the magnitude of decline in average daily hits per ATM between 2013 and 2018. States are color-coded by legend. Regional groupings are defined in the exhibit.
exhibits.data: Legend: 30 hits decline (darkest), 20 hits, 10 hits, 0 hits (constant), <0 hits (increase). Regions defined: Northeast (CT, ME, MA, NH, RI, VT, NJ, NY, PA), Midwest (IL, IN, MI, OH, WI, IA, KS, MN, MO, NE, ND, SD), South-Atlantic (DE, FL, GA, MD, NC, SC, VA, DC, WV), South-Central (AL, KY, MS, TN, AR, LA, OK, TX), West-Mountain (AZ, CO, ID, MT, NV, NM, UT, WY), West-Pacific (AK, CA, HI, OR, WA).

exhibits.title: Operating Costs for American Bank ATMs (2018)
exhibits.shows: A table showing the number of ATMs by region and operating structure (BO-BO, BO-VO, VO-VO), along with the daily operating cost to the bank per ATM for each structure. Notes clarify which party (owner vs. operator) is responsible for which costs.
exhibits.data: Daily cost to bank: BO-BO = $100, BO-VO = $60, VO-VO = $0. ATM counts by region: Northeast (250 BO-BO, 750 BO-VO, 1000 VO-VO), Midwest (1000, 800, 200), South-Atlantic (1500, 250, 250), South-Central (1500, 350, 150), West-Mountain (1200, 500, 300), West-Pacific (0, 500, 1500). Owner pays rent and utilities; Operator pays for maintenance and cash management.

exhibits.title: Reasons for Reduction in Hits in Vendor Operated ATMs
exhibits.shows: Three scatter plots for vendor-operated ATMs: (1) Price correlation — price per transaction vs. number of daily transactions; (2) Uptime correlation — uptime % vs. number of daily transactions; (3) Competition correlation — number of competitors in vicinity vs. number of daily transactions.
exhibits.data: Price: transactions range 94–101 as price ranges $0.99–$1.02, showing negligible correlation. Note: American Bank cannot reduce transaction prices further. Uptime: strong positive correlation — uptime of 70% yields ~70 transactions, uptime of 100% yields ~110 transactions. Competition: weak/no correlation — 0 competitors at ~85 txns, 4 competitors also at ~100 txns. Uptime definition: % of time ATM is functional; Downtime = 100% minus Uptime.

exhibits.title: Downtime Pattern and Causes in Vendor Operated ATMs
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing average uptime vs. downtime % for vendor-operated ATMs from 2014 to 2018, and a pie chart of downtime causes in 2018.
exhibits.data: Downtime has increased from near 0% in 2014 to approximately 20% in 2018 (uptime fell to ~80%). Downtime causes (2018): Cash-out (Operator) 25%, Power outage (Owner) 20%, Machine tech problems (Operator) 50%, Other technical issues (Operator) 5%. Operator is responsible for 80% of downtime causes.

exhibits.title: Revenues from ATMs (2018)
exhibits.shows: A table showing revenue earned by American Bank per hit, broken down by customer type (Own vs. Other), operating structure (BO-BO, BO-VO, VO-VO), and transaction type (Financial vs. Non-financial). Also shows average daily hits by region and operating structure split by financial and non-financial hits. Own:Other customer ratio is 1:1.
exhibits.data: Revenue per hit — Own customer: BO-BO Fin $2.0 / Non-fin $1.5; BO-VO Fin $1.5 / Non-fin $1.0; VO-VO Fin $1.0 / Non-fin $0.5. Other customer: BO-BO Fin $2.5 / Non-fin $2.0; BO-VO Fin $2.0 / Non-fin $1.5; VO-VO Fin $1.5 / Non-fin $1.0. Note: Own customer revenue = estimated savings vs. branch visit. VO-VO revenue is after deducting vendor commissions. Daily hits (Fin/Non-fin): Northeast BO-BO 12/10, BO-VO 12/8, VO-VO 8/12; Midwest BO-BO 127/173, BO-VO 97/73, VO-VO 48/62; South-Atlantic BO-BO 43/57, BO-VO 22/48, VO-VO 56/34; South-Central BO-BO 35/55, BO-VO 35/20, VO-VO 15/40; West-Mountain BO-BO 32/48, BO-VO 21/16, VO-VO 19/11; West-Pacific BO-BO 0/0, BO-VO 18/2, VO-VO 6/14.

exhibits.title: Metrics Comparison with Competition (2018)
exhibits.shows: Two stacked bar charts comparing American Bank with three competitors (PNK Bank, Townbank, Bells Cargo): (1) Proportion of Own vs. Other customers; (2) Proportion of Financial vs. Non-financial transactions.
exhibits.data: American Bank: ~50% Own / ~50% Other customers; ~45% Financial / ~55% Non-financial transactions. PNK Bank: higher share of financial transactions (~65%). Bells Cargo: higher share of Other customers (~70%). Best-in-class: 65% financial transactions (PNK Bank), 70% Other customers (Bells Cargo).

framework: Revenues falling: (a) Average transaction price falling — overall prices decreased or mix shifted toward cheaper transactions; (b) Fewer customers using ATMs — decrease in overall volume, higher-revenue own customers not using, customers moving to competitors or substitutes such as online banking; (c) No newer revenue sources introduced beyond core transaction revenues

Costs increasing: (a) Average variable cost of operating increased — cost per ATM increased or shift toward more expensive operating structures; (b) Fixed costs increased — cost of purchasing new ATMs increased

questions.prompt: What do Exhibit 1 data tell you about the nature of the profitability problem?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) Hits (transactions) are falling — total daily hits dropped from 96 to 85 per ATM over 5 years; (2) Other customers represent a smaller and declining share of hits; (3) Both revenue and profit declined, but operating costs appear constant (revenue and profit decline in parallel), implying the problem is revenue-side / volume-driven, not cost-driven.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, which regions show the most significant decline in ATM hits?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify the Northeast and West-Pacific regions as showing the largest declines (darkest shading on the map, approximately 30 hits decline). This directs the investigation toward those two regions.

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 3, what do you notice about the operating structure in the two problem regions (Northeast and West-Pacific)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that Northeast and West-Pacific are heavily concentrated in vendor-operated ATMs (BO-VO and VO-VO), unlike other regions which are dominated by BO-BO. This points to vendor-operated ATMs as the likely source of the hit decline.

questions.prompt: Exhibit 4 shows three potential reasons for the decline in hits at vendor-operated ATMs. What do you conclude?
questions.guidance: Candidate should analyze each scatter plot: (1) Price — no meaningful correlation and American Bank cannot lower prices further; (2) Uptime — strong positive correlation, suggesting downtime is the key driver; (3) Competition — no significant correlation. Conclusion: improving uptime is the most actionable lever.

questions.prompt: Exhibit 5 shows the downtime trend and its causes. How much can vendor management improve uptime, and what is the additional revenue impact?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) Downtime has risen ~20% over 5 years (from near 0% to ~20%); (2) Operator is responsible for 80% of downtime causes; (3) Vendor management can therefore address 80% of the 25% potential improvement = 20% uptime improvement; (4) 20% uptime improvement = 20 additional daily hits per vendor-operated ATM. Candidate should allocate the 20 new hits proportionally per exhibit 6 ratios and calculate revenue.

math.setup: 20% uptime improvement => 20 additional daily hits per vendor-operated ATM in Northeast and West-Pacific. Allocate 20 new hits proportionally to Fin/Non-fin using existing ratios from Exhibit 6. Average revenue per hit = 0.5*Own_rev + 0.5*Other_rev (1:1 ratio).
steps: Northeast BO-VO: 20 new hits split 12 Fin / 8 Non-fin (same ratio). Revenue = [12*$1.75 + 8*$1.25] * 750 ATMs = [$21+$10]*750 = $31*750 = $23,250
Northeast VO-VO: 20 new hits split 8 Fin / 12 Non-fin. Revenue = [8*$1.25 + 12*$0.75] * 1000 ATMs = [$10+$9]*1000 = $19*1000 = $19,000
West-Pacific BO-VO: 20 new hits split 18 Fin / 2 Non-fin. Revenue = [18*$1.75 + 2*$1.25] * 500 ATMs = [$31.5+$2.5]*500 = $34*500 = $17,000
West-Pacific VO-VO: 20 new hits split 6 Fin / 14 Non-fin. Revenue = [6*$1.25 + 14*$0.75] * 1500 ATMs = [$7.5+$10.5]*1500 = $18*1500 = $27,000
math.answer: $86,250 additional daily revenue potential from managing vendors to eliminate operator-caused downtime in Northeast and West-Pacific.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 6A, how much additional revenue could American Bank earn by improving its customer mix and transaction mix to best-in-class competitor levels?
questions.guidance: Candidate should benchmark American Bank against best-in-class: Bells Cargo has 70% Other customers vs. 50% for American Bank (20pp gap); PNK Bank has 65% Financial transactions vs. 45% for American Bank (20pp gap). Since Other customers earn $0.5 more per hit and Financial transactions earn $0.5 more per hit, candidate should compute the blended uplift per hit and multiply across total hits.

math.setup: American Bank: 50% Other customers, 45% Fin txns. Best-in-class: 70% Other (Bells Cargo), 65% Fin (PNK Bank). Gap: +20pp Other, +20pp Fin. Extra revenue per hit from each improvement = $0.5 (from Exhibit 6 revenue table differentials). Total hits = 85 per ATM * 12,000 ATMs = 1,020,000 daily hits.
steps: Segment the hit base into 4 buckets by customer type x transaction type using current 50/50 and 45/55 ratios

Additional revenue from shifting 20% of hits to Other customers: affects 80% non-financial (Own->Other +$0.5) and 20% financial (Own->Other +$0.5): 20%*80%*$0.5 + 20%*20%*($0.5+$0.5) = $0.08+$0.04 = $0.12 ... or simplified: 20%*$0.5 = $0.10 per hit from other-customer improvement

Additional revenue from shifting 20% of hits to Financial transactions: affects 80% Other (non-fin->fin +$0.5) and 20% Own (non-fin->fin +$0.5): 20%*80%*$0.5 + 20%*20%*$0.5 = $0.08+$0.04... simplified: 20%*$0.5 = $0.10 per hit
Combined blended uplift per hit = $0.08 + $0.04 + $0.00 + $0.08 = $0.20 per hit (per casebook matrix method)
math.answer: $204,000 additional daily revenue potential from improving Other customer and Financial transaction proportions to best-in-class competitor levels.

questions.prompt: [Interviewer-led, optional] What is the average break-even number of daily hits for bank-owned ATMs? Assume Fin:Non-fin and Own:Other ratios are both 1:1.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize VO-VO ATMs have $0 operating cost to the bank (not relevant for break-even). Only BO-BO ($100/day) and BO-VO ($60/day) matter. With 1:1:1:1 split across four customer-type x transaction-type buckets, average revenue per hit is the simple average of all four bucket revenues.

math.setup: Assume Fin:Non-fin = 1:1 and Own:Other = 1:1. Break-even hits = Daily operating cost / Average revenue per hit. Average rev per hit = 0.25*(Own Fin + Own Non-fin + Other Fin + Other Non-fin).
math.answer: Break-even is 50 daily hits for BO-BO ATMs and 40 daily hits for BO-VO ATMs. VO-VO ATMs have no operating cost to the bank, so any hit is profitable.

brainstorming.prompt: What other actions can American Bank take to improve profitability of loss-making ATMs (after exhausting hit-improvement levers)?

categories.name: Revenue enhancement
ideas: Add new ATM functionalities (check deposit, cash deposit, bill payment) to drive more transaction types
Allocate intangible brand/marketing value to ATMs in prime locations
Introduce advertising on ATM screens to generate non-transaction revenue
Partner with other financial institutions to allow their customers to use American Bank ATMs for a fee

categories.name: Cost reduction / structure
ideas: Negotiate lower operating fees or service-level agreements with vendors
Convert expensive BO-VO ATMs to VO-VO where feasible to eliminate bank operating cost
Renegotiate vendor contracts to shift more downtime responsibility costs to vendors

categories.name: Network optimization
ideas: Relocate underperforming ATMs to higher-traffic locations
Consolidate or shut down loss-making ATMs with no path to profitability
Sell off surplus ATMs to vendors or competitors

categories.name: Mix and channel optimization
ideas: Run targeted campaigns to increase proportion of Other customers using American Bank ATMs
Incentivize own customers to conduct more financial transactions (e.g., transfers, payments) at ATMs
Invest in digital integration so ATM sessions naturally lead to financial transactions

recommendation: Improve vendor management practices and renegotiate vendor contracts in the Northeast and West-Pacific regions to eliminate operator-caused downtime (responsible for 80% of the 20% uptime shortfall), potentially recovering $86,250 in daily revenue.

Increase the proportion of Other customers and Financial transactions to best-in-class competitor levels (Bells Cargo at 70% Other, PNK Bank at 65% Financial) through targeted marketing and ATM capability enhancements, potentially adding $204,000 in daily revenue.
Total daily revenue and profit improvement potential: $290,250 with no incremental operating cost.
risks: Costs to manage vendors and renegotiate contracts may be significant, potentially eroding the $86,250 revenue gain.
Marketing spend to shift customer and transaction mix may be material and could reduce or eliminate the $204,000 gain.
Greater ATM usage could cannibalize branch traffic, leading to branch staffing reductions and associated people-management challenges.
Overinvestment in ATM channel may divert resources from faster-growing digital and online banking channels.
next_steps: Begin auditing vendor contracts in Northeast and West-Pacific to identify SLA gaps and renegotiation opportunities.
Identify specific loss-making ATMs (below break-even of 50 hits for BO-BO or 40 hits for BO-VO) and evaluate relocation, repurposing, or closure.
Study customer usage patterns in detail to design targeted campaigns that improve Other customer proportion and Financial transaction mix.
